items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: And Lorenzo Starr played with me.

ctx.x: Well, let's talk on about some of the other three parts. Okay, right out. What about banjo players? Who were some of the good ones?

Well, the one who played with me was pretty good, I know, Gallier. He played with me. And Lorenzo Starr played with me. Tom Benton played with me. And I wouldn't say that it was the best, Dick. I couldn't say that because, you know, a whole lot of them playing a lot of banjo around here. So I just couldn't say it was the best. But I know I liked the bloody name better than them Gallier. I liked his Gallier.
What kind of a fella was he, Gallier?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: Well, a couple of times Lorenzo Stahl played with us too.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, I met him once. Yeah, Tom Benton.
Where's the other one? Well, a couple of times Lorenzo Stahl played with us too.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Willie Connish, and Lurens of Stahl on guitar.

ctx.x: And what was Bill Matthews playing? Trombone or playing drums?

No, no, no, he wasn't playing trombone then. I forgot now what he was playing. But he didn't have, that's right, he didn't have them at the same time. He didn't have Bill, I mean, at the same time. Because he was playing trombone, he was playing trombone, Willie Connish, Willie Connish, and Lurens of Stahl on guitar. They didn't use but five pieces. No piano. No piano. No saxophone. No saxophone. No saxophone. No saxophone. Tuxedo band, the only band used a piano. And they have a piano when they go to a place to…
Now what about in playing trumpet behind the singers? How did that develop?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1971-04-08
items.q: And Lorenzo said, look out there. He said, you better watch out, say, there's somebody gonna get you.

ctx.x: Baby Dots, isn't it? Yeah, go ahead.

Oh, sure. Baby Dots. And, uh... So somebody made me acquainted with Ori. I don't know who it was, but... And he asked me to come up and blow some. This is... This is no joke. This is real. So I went up and blowed. I blowed me some army numbers. I blowed me some blues, and I blowed me some songs, you know. So they said, oh, yeah. And Lorenzo said, look out there. He said, you better watch out, say, there's somebody gonna get you. And Lorenzo said to him, well, let him get me. That's all right. I quit. I quit. And…
Yeah. When did you learn Smiles Bunch?
